verification_report.summary:
The full supplied section passes sequential verification relative to the expressly accepted inputs. Thirteen statement-check records and six reference-check records cover the preparatory lemmas, the complete theorem proof, and the explanatory statements. No critical errors or gaps were found. At final inspection, common_barrier_compactness_01 had no completed verification report; as requested, cor:common-barrier-continuity and lem:fixed-npp-integrals are accepted conditionally. Their applications here satisfy their stated hypotheses. This verdict does not independently certify that pending prerequisite.

The arbitrary-background mixed inequality is valid. Freezing gives closed positive local Hessians dd^c(u+q) and dd^c(v+q), with the required top-power lower bounds. Writing dV=h dLeb converts the measurable densities correctly. Positivity transfers the local result to theta+2eta kappa and then to theta+2C eta omega. The fixed finite atlas gives C independent of eta. The finite polynomial expansion of bounded products justifies the final limit. No closedness or positivity of the original theta is assumed.

The fixed-reference trace estimate is uniform in the oscillation of normalized v. Positivity first replaces theta_psi by Omega_psi, and bounded Stokes has the displayed positive sign. For m=n-1, differentiating (Omega+dd^c psi)^m gives coefficients m and m(m-1), hence exactly (n-1)(n-2) in the torsion term. Smooth torsion forms are dominated by the indicated positive mixed measures. Fixed local corrections reduce their integrals against |v| to weighted CLN, giving dependence on ||v||L1 rather than ||v||infinity. Normalized compactness supplies the uniform L1 bound. The accepted bounded current and weighted continuity calculus justifies the rough identities and limits. For n=2 only dd^c Omega remains; for n=1 the trace is integral theta by Stokes.

For smooth positive f, exact Hermitian regularization supplies uniformly bounded psi_j decreasing to psi. The genuine rooftops satisfy psi<=q_j<=psi_j and decrease to psi. Contact support, positive background enlargement, and ordered contact yield the displayed bound by Omega_psi_j^n. Thus each rooftop measure has a bounded measurable smooth-volume density; individual noncollapse makes it nonzero. The accepted big-background Lp theorem applies separately to each density. The two exponential barriers have the correct signs and give uniform bounds without uniform density norms or uniform positive lower masses. In the capacity corollary, reference zero is admissible because P_(delta theta)(0)=0. Bounded weighted capacity continuity passes the equation to the limit.

For general bounded nu-measurable f, finite Radon regularity gives continuous L1(nu) approximants. Clamp them before smooth uniform approximation, then add a vanishing positive constant: this supplies smooth strictly positive f_j with a common upper bound and the required convergence. The fixed lower barrier psi-C follows from exponential order. For each fixed j, the inner approximants have measurable densities relative to smooth volume. Applying the proved mixed lemma gives exactly exp(lambda u_(j,k)/n) f_j^(1/n) MA_theta(q_k). Their common bounds and capacity convergence justify both mixed-product and weighted-measure limits. No mixed inequality for arbitrary singular measures is imported.

The normalization contradiction is valid even though osc(v_j) may diverge. Normalized compactness gives a genuine limit v with supremum zero. The conditional exponential-integral lemma requires only a common upper bound, which v_j<=0 supplies. The root inequality and Holder give convergence of the density roots in L1(nu). Since integral f dnu>0 and nu ignores the pole set of v, the limiting weighted root integral is strictly positive. Integrating the mixed inequality and applying the fixed-reference trace yields a exp(lambda M_j/n)<=C_psi, contradicting M_j tending to infinity. This argument also works in dimension one.

The resulting two-sided bounds give domination by one fixed finite non-pluripolar measure and hence the final capacity and weak Monge-Ampere convergence. The displayed two-term estimate, together with fixed-measure exponential convergence, proves total-variation convergence of the right sides. Bounded exponential order gives uniqueness, including where f vanishes. If mu were zero, individual noncollapse would rule out a bounded solution. Bigness is used through the accepted genuine-current noncollapse, order and Lp existence inputs; analytic singularities are never assumed. No BMP, PVP, continuous smooth-volume density, or mass bound for all bounded potentials enters.

The references were searched first with search_arxiv_theorems and then checked in the cited primary versions. [Dinew, Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0705.0974v1) is the required bounded local result with L1 Lebesgue densities. Its normalization rescales both sides equally, so the book's dd^c=i/(2pi) partial barpartial introduces no missing factor. [Nguyen, Lemma 1.9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891v1) matches the Hermitian special case; its operator is twice the book's, handled by halving reference potentials. [ALS, Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1) matches the reconstruction attribution and is not imported as proof. The manuscript correctly avoids the source's printed n(n-1) torsion coefficient. The internal weighted CLN citation and book conventions are accurate. Book files were accessed read-only.
